text:
Maya: kicking off a 72h soak/load run for the new eu-central-3 cluster — targeting LLM serving fleet (a mix of A100s + T4s). starting 12:30 UTC. goal: validate autoscaler config and warmup patterns before handoff to oncall. :rocket:
Alex: +1. can you paste the autoscaler config you're testing? want to compare to earlier region defaults.
Maya: here it is (edited to highlight diffs):
```yaml
policy: request_based
metric: p50_token_latency_ms
scale_up_threshold: 180
scale_down_threshold: 90
min_replicas: 4
max_replicas: 80
cooldown_seconds: 240
prewarm_replicas: 6   # warm pool to keep KV cache warm
burst_capacity: 12    # allows short spikes
node_selector: gpu-type=a100
```
Sanjay: a few notes:
- p50 is okay for aggressive cost/latency tradeoffs but watch p95 for tail spikes. we usually autoscale on a mix of queue_length and gpu_util to avoid noisy-unicorns.
- Prewarm pool is crucial for cache hit ratio. confirm prewarm node lifecycle doesn't evict too often.
Liam: also confirm scale_down cooldown >= model load time. if nodes boot and pull checkpoints for 6m, cooldown 240s will oscillate. increase to 420s for A100 jobs.
Maya: good call — bumping cooldown to 420s for the A100 nodegroup. leaving T4 pools with 240s.
Alex: load generator plan? are we doing synthetic token streams or real prompt mix?
Maya: running 2 streams in parallel:
1) synthetic: steady QPS targeting 60% avg GPU util (to validate batching)
2) production-sample: replay of ~10k user prompts (varied lengths) to exercise KV cache and model fetch.
Using our harness:
```bash
./harness/run_load.sh --region eu-central-3 --qps 120 --duration 72h --mix production.sample.json
```
infra-bot: NOTICE: new cluster eu-central-3 provisioned (node pools: a100-16, t4-32). storage bw: 12GiB/s. networking: 10Gbps per-host.
Sanjay: monitoring to watch: p50/p95 latency, GPU_util, batch_size_mean, queue_length, model_fetch_rate, disk_io_wait, pod_eviction_rate, node_creation_time, egress_cost_estimate.
Alex: propose these alert thresholds for the soak (notify eng-runtime, eng-sre):
- p95 generation latency > 1200ms for 5m -> SEV-3
- GPU_util > 95% for 10m -> performance risk, scale_up recommended
- average batch_size < 3 for 15m -> batching not working
- failed model fetches > 0.5% for 10m -> investigate registry/network
Maya: added. also flag for unexpected scaling oscillation: >3 scale cycles within 15m -> auto-roll to canary fallback.
Liam: cost note: if we keep prewarm_replicas=6 for A100 for 72h that's ~6 * 24 * 3 = ~432 GPU-hours. rough cost impact ~ $X/day (we'll attach precise billing after run). consider reducing prewarm after 24h if stability proven.
Maya: plan for ramp:
- hour 0-1: 10% target qps (smoke)
- hour 1-6: linear ramp to 60%
- hour 6-24: hold at 60%
- day 2: run production-sample replay at peak for 3x baseline to test fallback
- day 3: scale down test and graceful shutdowns
Sanjay: add network partition test (short 2m drop between control plane and nodes) to validate fallback. schedule at non-peak.
Maya: scheduled partition test at hour 30. will annotate in run log.
Alex: autoscaler tuning suggestions from previous region: switch to dual-metric rule to reduce jitter:
```yaml
rules:
  - condition: gpu_util > 80% AND queue_length > 10 -> scale_up by 25%
  - condition: gpu_util < 30% AND queue_length == 0 -> scale_down by 15% (min wait 420s)
```
Maya: implemented. also enabled 'graceful_drain': true to give in-flight batches time to finish.
infra-bot: ALERT (simulated): node a100-16-12 rebooted during bootstrap (kernel panic) — flagged but node rejoined after 45s.
Liam: log snippet from node kernel: `oom_killer invoked for containerd` — need to check kubelet memory thresholds for the nodegroup.
Sanjay: reduce kube-reserved for the a100-16 pool by 2Gi and retry, plus set evictionHard to 1Gi for pods with large cache.
Maya: ack, updated. we saw a small spike in model_fetch_rate during the first hour (cold pulls) — cache hit went from 2% -> 62% after prewarm filled.
Alex: how did batching behave? mean batch_size?
Maya: mean batch_size (A100 pool) climbed to 8 during steady 60% util, queue length peaked at 18 during peak tests, p95 stayed ~980ms. p50 ~120ms.
Liam: that's reasonable. watch for tail during large prompt replays.
Maya: on day2 when we ran 3x peak replay, autoscaler scaled up to 68 replicas (within max) and latency p95 jumped to 1.8s briefly then recovered after burst_capacity engaged.
Sanjay: confirm burst_capacity only on A100 pool? if T4s are compatible they can take low-latency short requests; else we pay for fallback.
Maya: burst only on A100 group for critical traffic. T4s used for background/cheap embeddings.
Alex: next: handoff checklist to eng-sre on successful soak:
- soak_run_id & runbook link in ops doc
- dashboard: p50/p95, gpu_util, batch size, queue_length, scale events timeline
- incidents: list of any node reboots / registry failures / partition tests and outcomes
- cost delta report (provisioning + egress) for test window
- recommended autoscaler tweaks (cooldowns, dual-metric thresholds, prewarm count)
Maya: will assemble and drop in #incidents and ops doc. aiming to handoff tomorrow EOD if stable.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout passed for model v2.1. Pinning model image across region: registry.redwood/models:v2.1
Alex: final thought — add a synthetic long-tail generator to exercise 8k+ token prompts sporadically (1% of traffic) so cache eviction + kv growth tested.
Maya: added tail generator. kickstarting run now. will post interim metrics every 6h. :eyes:
Liam: thanks team. if anything looks broken ping oncall and add SEV tag.
Maya: closing thread for now — will update with 6h snapshot.
